slides.title: The Big Sky
bullets: Prepare to read, discuss and write
slides.narration: Welcome to Grade 2 English, Unit 4: The Big Sky. Look up! In this unit you learn the words for everything in the big sky: the sun, the moon, the stars, the clouds and your own shadow. You find out why a shadow is long in the morning and short at midday, and why we have day and night. You collect describing words for the sky and the weather, you write true sky facts in the present simple, and you use verbs ending in -ed to tell what you saw last night. Along the way you read “The Night Amal Counted the Stars” and wonder about the world, just as Amal does. In this short lecture, preview the key ideas and prepare for the independent lesson.

slides.title: What you will achieve
bullets: Name the things you can see in the sky: the sun, the moon, the stars and the clouds.
Say what a shadow is and explain how it forms when something blocks the light.
Talk about how the sky changes in the morning, at midday and in the evening.
slides.narration: By the end of this unit, you will be able to name the things you can see in the sky: the sun, the moon, the stars and the clouds. You will also say what a shadow is and explain how it forms when something blocks the light. You will also talk about how the sky changes in the morning, at midday and in the evening. Keep these goals in mind as you work.

slides.title: Words to learn
slides.narration: Your vocabulary work begins with these words: light, bright, high, sight, air, fire. Listen to each word, look at what it means, and try to use it when you talk and write.

slides.title: Read and think
bullets: Point to the words that show it
slides.narration: The reading sequence includes A Poem: “My Shadow” and Telling Time with a Shadow. Read slowly, look at the pictures, and find the big idea in each text. When you answer a question, point to the words that show it.

Try it in your own sentences
slides.narration: The first language focus is Describing Words (Adjectives). An adjective is a describing word. It tells us more about a noun, which is a person, a place or a thing. Adjectives help you paint a clear picture of the sky, the sun and your own shadow. Look at the examples, then try the pattern in your own sentences.

slides.title: Use English for a real purpose
bullets: Say it, write it, make it better
slides.narration: In speaking, you will complete Speaking 1 — Describe the Sky. Say your ideas clearly and listen to your partner. In writing, you will draw, trace, copy or write, then check your work with a grown-up or the AI tutor.

slides.title: You are ready to begin
bullets: Activities, quiz and optional live sessions
slides.narration: You are ready to begin. Start with the words, then the reading and the questions, then the grammar, speaking and writing. Ask the AI tutor for help any time, and bring your questions to a live session too if you join one.
